leftEvidence.title: Adonijah advances while David is old

points.label: Action and response
points.left: David’s age, Abishag’s service, Adonijah’s self-exaltation, invited supporters, excluded figures, and Nathan and Bathsheba’s coordinated appeal bring the succession crisis to the king.
points.right: David tells Solomon to be strong, keep the LORD’s charge, and deal wisely with Joab, Barzillai’s sons, and Shimei; he dies, is buried, and Solomon’s throne is established.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places silence about succession allows a rival claim to gather publicly inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places Torah language, unresolved relationships, death, and succession meet in the final charge inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Kings 1:1–27 and 1 Kings 2:1–12 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Succession, Retelling, and Temple Preparation” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.
payload.tension: 1 Kings 1:1–27 foregrounds silence about succession allows a rival claim to gather publicly; 1 Kings 2:1–12 foregrounds Torah language, unresolved relationships, death, and succession meet in the final charge. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
payload.title: Adonijah advances while David is old / David charges Solomon and dies
